sources.title: Transus meets Hornbach's requirement with EDI and SSCC label service
Customer case: Henri van de Bilt (VMI for Albert Heijn)
Arjan Sloot new Managing Director at Transus

items.title: Retailer mandates are the main trigger for supplier adoption
items.summary: Transus names three reasons to adopt EDI: a retailer mandates it, an ERP migration, and coming e-invoicing mandates. Anova Seafood: "If you want to participate as a supplier, you need to work with EDI"; Hornbach made EDI and SSCC labels mandatory for suppliers.
items.implication: Acquisition follows retailer programmes; retailer profiles and fast connection matter more than features.

items.title: The network is the moat: 100,000+ partners and connection in about a day
items.summary: Transus states more than 100,000 connected trading partners in 40+ countries and that simple connections are often live within 24 hours; Anova reports adding a retailer at no extra cost within 24 hours.
items.implication: Directory coverage and onboarding speed are the core value metrics; keep them measurable per connection.

items.title: Flat pricing removes volume anxiety
items.summary: Plans include unlimited messages and trading partners at a fixed monthly price: Basic from EUR 79 and Plus from EUR 149 per month on annual terms (EUR 99/189 monthly), Premium on request.
items.implication: Revenue grows with customers and plan upgrades, not volume; the business must keep cost-to-serve per connection low (automation, Traci AI).

items.title: German e-invoicing obligations create a 2027-2028 demand wave
items.summary: Germany requires receiving e-invoices since 2025, sending from 1 January 2027 for companies above EUR 800,000 turnover and for all from 2028, in XRechnung, ZUGFeRD 2.1+ or via Peppol (EN 16931). Transus supports these with Tickstar.
items.implication: E-invoicing is the strongest near-term growth lever for customers trading with Germany.

items.title: NIS2 pushes security assurance into the sales cycle
items.summary: Customers classified as essential or important entities under NIS2 assess Transus as a supplier. Transus reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, encryption in transport (TLS/AS2/SFTP), Frankfurt hosting with Amsterdam DR, annual pentests and an incident response plan; it is not itself in NIS2 scope.
items.implication: A ready assurance pack shortens enterprise deals; continuity and incident reporting become product features.

items.title: AI-assisted mapping targets the slowest step
items.summary: Traci AI recognises and links trading documents automatically to remove manual mapping that "often takes days or even weeks".
items.implication: If it works at scale, onboarding cost falls and self-service becomes possible; specialist review remains needed for low-confidence cases (inference).

items.title: Validation and shared visibility build trust on both sides
items.summary: Messages with errors are blocked automatically with an alert explained in understandable language, and trading partners can log in to view message status even if they are not customers.
items.implication: Exception handling is a differentiator for non-IT users; monitoring belongs in the core product.

items.title: Transus is the B2B connectivity layer of the Katapull Commerce Hub
items.summary: Katapull presents eight labels (Vendit, Logic4, Highbiza, EffectConnect, DeliveryMatch, Transus, Returnista, Picqer), 4,500+ customers in 40+ countries and 175+ specialists. Transus lists each sibling as a Commerce Hub partner that "can be connected with Transus". An interim Transus MD came from Katapull from February 2026.
items.implication: Cross-selling EDI into sibling customer bases and productised connectors are a strategic growth path; the acquisition date is not publicly confirmed in the sources reviewed.

items.title: VMI extends EDI from transactions into collaboration
items.summary: Henri van de Bilt uses Transus VMI to replenish Albert Heijn from forecasts and stock data, sending DESADV to AH and XPO Logistics, to deliver fresher product.
items.implication: Collaboration services raise switching costs and value beyond message delivery.
